mainTopic: Whether someone who pledges a specific animal or house to הקדש must pay if it is lost. This passage first finishes the previous discussion about a pledge made before death.
overview: This amud opens by finishing the previous sugya. Once a person has stood in court (עמד בדין), his property is already tied to the pledge, so his heirs must pay even if the assessment comes after he dies. A new משנה then teaches the following. If someone says 'this bull is an עולה,' he owes nothing if it dies. If he says 'this bull is upon me (עלי) as an עולה,' he must pay. רבי חייא בר רב limits the second case to someone who pledged the bull's value (דמי). A ברייתא seems to say otherwise, so the גמרא reads it as a case of דמי too. It explains the two clauses of the ברייתא as two ways of pledging value: making the bull holy for its value, or making holy the money from its future sale. Making holy that future money only works for רבי מאיר, who holds אדם מקדיש דבר שלא בא לעולם. A second version reaches the same conclusion as a question and answer. The amud ends by quoting a ברייתא about a rented house struck with נגעים, which some attach this discussion to; that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Standing in court ties up his property even before the assessment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what the earlier ruling teaches. Once the person stood in court, his property became tied to the debt. The later assessment only reveals an amount that was already owed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since they never assessed him, his property was never tied to the debt. So the ruling teaches us: since he stood in court, his property was already tied to it. The assessment just reveals what was already true.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the previous discussion. It explains which wrong idea the earlier ruling (that the heirs pay) is meant to rule out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the debt only becomes real once the amount is fixed by an assessment. If so, a person who died before being assessed would leave his heirs owing nothing. The גמרא says no: standing in court (עמד בדין) is what creates the lien, and the assessment (אומדנא) only reveals the amount.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: introduces the mistaken idea being ruled out
It teaches us: introduces the new point
His property became tied to (liened for) the debt
Stood in judgment before the court
The assessment or estimate of value
Merely revealing something that was already true

steps.whatToRemember: Standing in court (עמד בדין) is what ties up the property. The assessment (אומדנא) only reveals the amount, so it can even be done after the person dies.

phrases.english: What might you have said?
Since they did not assess it
his property was not tied to the debt,
so it teaches us:
since he stood in judgment,
his property was indeed tied to the debt,
and the assessment is merely revealing the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the discussion from the previous part of the daf by explaining why the earlier ruling was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the new point: what false idea the ruling rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without an assessment, the property is not tied to the debt, so the heirs are exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Standing in court ties up the property. The assessment only reveals the amount.

steps.title: Consecrating this specific bull or house: exempt if it is lost
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on someone who directly consecrates a specific bull or house. If it dies or collapses, he does not have to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'This bull is an עולה' or 'This house is a קרבן,' and the bull died or the house fell down, he does not have to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Its first case is where the item itself was consecrated, with no personal promise attached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He made the object itself holy but took no obligation on himself. So once the object is gone, nothing remains for him to owe.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A burnt offering
An offering (here, something given to הקדש)
Exempt from paying

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If one says: "This bull is a burnt offering,"
or "This house is an offering,"
and the bull died or the house collapsed,
he is exempt from paying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrating a specific item, without saying 'upon me,' creates no personal obligation. If the item is lost, he owes nothing.

steps.title: Saying 'upon me': obligated to pay if it is lost
steps.stepSummary: If he adds the word 'upon me' (עלי), he has to pay when the bull dies or the house collapses.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'This bull is upon me as an עולה' or 'This house is upon me as a קרבן,' and the bull died or the house fell down, he must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second case, which is the opposite of the first. Adding 'upon me' makes him liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עלי ('upon me') turns the pledge into a personal obligation. Losing the item does not cancel a duty that rests on him.

keyTerms.meaning: Upon me: a personal obligation
Obligated to pay

steps.whatToRemember: With no 'upon me,' he owes nothing if the item is lost. With 'upon me' (עלי), he must pay.

phrases.english: But if one says: "This bull is upon me as a burnt offering,"
or "This house is upon me as an offering,"
and the bull died or the house collapsed,
he is obligated to pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The contrasting second half of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'upon me' makes him responsible to pay if the item is lost.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר רב limits the משנה to pledging the bull's value
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר רב says the משנה only makes him liable when he said 'the value (דמי) of this bull is upon me.' If he said just 'this bull is upon me,' he only meant he must bring it, so he is not liable if it dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר רב said: the משנה only taught this where he said 'the value of this bull is upon me as an עולה.' But if he said 'this bull is upon me as an עולה,' then since he said 'this' and it died, he is not responsible. He only meant 'I must bring it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with an אמורא narrowing the second case of the משנה. He says it is really talking about pledging the money value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'this' (זה) points to one specific animal. So 'upon me' only obligates him to bring that animal, not to replace it. Only pledging its value (דמי) creates a money obligation that survives the animal's death.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
They only taught this in the case where: a limiting phrase
The value (price) of
Responsibility to replace something if it is lost
It is upon me to bring it (only to deliver it)

steps.confusionAlert: The printed משנה says 'this bull is upon me,' but רבי חייא בר רב reads it as if the person said 'the value of this bull is upon me.'

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Chiyya bar Rav says:
They taught this only where he said:
"The value of this bull is upon me as a burnt offering."
But if he said: "This bull is upon me as a burnt offering,"
since he said "this" and it died,
he is not responsible for its loss,
for he is saying: "It is upon me to bring it."
phrases.notes: He means 'upon me' was only a promise to deliver this particular bull, not to pay for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the case in step 3 of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is liability only when he pledged the value (דמי). Saying 'this bull is upon me' only obligates him to bring it.

steps.title: A ברייתא says 'this bull is upon me' does create responsibility
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא בר רב from a ברייתא. It says that 'this bull is upon me as an עולה' makes him responsible if the bull dies or is stolen, even though he never mentioned its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected from a ברייתא. 'This bull is an עולה': the bull is holy and מעילה applies to it, and if it died or was stolen he is not responsible. 'This bull is upon me as an עולה': the bull is holy and מעילה applies to it, and if it died or was stolen he is responsible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to directly contradict רבי חייא בר רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר רב said that 'this bull is upon me' only obligates him to bring it, so he is not liable if it dies. The ברייתא says the exact words 'this bull is upon me' do make him liable. It never mentions דמי (value), which contradicts his limitation.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated property
One who uses it for personal benefit is liable for מְעִילָה (misusing holy property)
Was stolen

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"This bull is a burnt offering":
the bull is consecrated, and one is liable for misusing it;
if it died or was stolen,
he is not responsible for its loss.
"This bull is upon me as a burnt offering":
the bull is consecrated, and one is liable for misusing it;
if it died or was stolen,
he is responsible for its loss.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא בר רב's claim that 'this bull is upon me' carries no responsibility
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly makes him responsible for 'this bull is upon me,' with no mention of its value.

steps.title: The ברייתא also means he said 'the value'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא, like the משנה, is talking about someone who said 'the value of this bull'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the ברייתא any stronger than our משנה, which we explained as a case where he said 'the value'? Here too, he said 'the value'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חייא בר רב. It reads the ברייתא the same way he read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the ברייתא was about someone who said only 'this bull is upon me'. The גמרא answers that if we could add 'דמי' to the משנה, we can add it to the ברייתא too. So the ברייתא no longer contradicts רבי חייא בר רב.

keyTerms.meaning: stronger; carries more weight
we established it as; we explained it as a case of

phrases.english: Is it stronger than our משנה,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא from the last step. The point is that the ברייתא has no more authority than the משנה.

phrases.english: which we established is where he says 'the value of'?
Here too, it is where he says 'the value of'.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source as a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about someone who said only 'this bull is upon me', which would contradict רבי חייא בר רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about someone who said 'the value of this bull', just like the משנה.

steps.title: The later clause says 'value', so the first clause did not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the סיפא of the ברייתא openly mentions 'דמי'. This suggests the רישא is a case without 'דמי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the last clause is where he says 'the value', the first clause must be where he does not say 'the value'. The last clause teaches: 'The value of a bull as an עולה': the bull stays non-holy and there is no מעילה with it. If it died or was stolen, he is not responsible for it. But he is responsible for its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 6. It uses the wording of the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא spells out the case of 'דמי' and gives it a different ruling: the bull itself is not holy, and he is not responsible if it dies. If the רישא were also about 'דמי', why would the ברייתא separate the two clauses with different rulings? So the רישא seems to be the plain 'this bull is upon me', which brings back the problem for רבי חייא בר רב.

keyTerms.meaning: the first clause of a teaching
the last clause of a teaching
non-holy, ordinary property

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two clauses. The רישא (step 5) makes him responsible for the bull itself. The סיפא makes him responsible only for its money value, not for the bull.

phrases.english: But since the last clause is where he says 'the value of',
the first clause must be where he does not say 'the value of'!
For the last clause teaches: 'The value of a bull as an עולה':
the bull is non-holy, and there is no misuse liability with it;

phrases.aramaic: מֵת אוֹ נִגְנַב — אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתוֹ,
phrases.english: if it died or was stolen, he is not responsible for it,
but he is responsible for its value!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִדְּסֵיפָא דְּקָאָמַר ״דְּמֵי״ רֵישָׁא דְּלָא קָאָמַר ״דְּמֵי״
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רישא of the ברייתא is a case of 'דמי'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא states 'דמי' openly and rules differently. That implies the רישא is not a case of 'דמי'.

steps.title: Both clauses say 'value', in two different ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both clauses involve 'דמי'. The רישא consecrates the bull for its value. The סיפא consecrates only the money that will come from selling it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both the first and last clauses are where he says 'the value'. The first clause is where he said, 'Let the bull become holy for its value.' The last clause is where he said, 'When its money comes, let it become holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps its reading that the רישא is about 'דמי'. It explains how the two clauses still differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא the bull itself becomes holy, so it can be sold for its value, and he is responsible if it dies. In the סיפא only the future sale money is holy. So the bull stays חולין and he is not responsible for it. This keeps רבי חייא בר רב's rule: he is only liable when he mentions 'דמי'.

keyTerms.meaning: let the bull become holy for its value
when its money (from the sale) comes
they will become holy

phrases.english: Both the first and last clauses are where he says 'the value of';
the first clause is where he said: 'Let the bull become holy for its value,'
and the last clause is where he said: 'When its money comes, let it become holy.'
phrases.notes: He means the money he will get later when he sells the bull.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling apart two forms of the same wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the סיפא mentions 'דמי', the רישא must be a case without it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both clauses mention 'דמי'. The רישא makes the bull holy for its value, while the סיפא makes only the future sale money holy.

steps.title: Can someone make holy something that does not exist yet?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the explanation of the סיפא. The sale money does not exist yet, and a person cannot make holy something not yet in existence.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a person cannot make holy something that has not yet come into the world!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new explanation of the סיפא from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the person in the סיפא made holy the money from a future sale. But that money does not exist yet. According to the known rule, his words should have no effect at all.

keyTerms.meaning: something that does not yet exist
makes holy; dedicates to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: But a person cannot make holy
something that has not yet come into the world?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֵין אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of the סיפא given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the סיפא as 'when its money comes, let it become holy'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The money does not exist yet, and one cannot make holy something not yet in existence.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב answers that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who holds that a person can make holy something not yet in existence.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Whose view is this? It is רבי מאיר, who says a person can make holy something that has not yet come into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by tying the ברייתא to a תנא who disagrees with that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'one cannot make holy something not yet in existence' is not agreed on by everyone. רבי מאיר holds that one can. Since the ברייתא follows his view, the explanation of the סיפא holds, and so does the defense of רבי חייא בר רב.

keyTerms.meaning: whose view is this?

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא בר רב is defended. Both the משנה and the ברייתא are cases where he said 'דמי'. The סיפא of the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who holds a person can make holy something not yet in existence.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one ruling in the ברייתא depends on a known disagreement about making holy things that do not exist yet.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Meir,
who says: A person can make holy
something that has not yet come into the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees one cannot make holy something not yet in existence, so the סיפא's case could not work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who allows making holy something not yet in existence.

steps.title: Another version: does the ברייתא follow רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב פפא asks אביי, or רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא, whether the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who holds that a person can make holy something not yet in existence.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it went like this. רב פפא said to אביי, and some say רמי בר חמא said to רב חסדא: Whose view does this ברייתא follow? Is it רבי מאיר, who says a person can make holy something that has not yet come into the world?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב's answer from Step 10. Here the same idea is asked as a question: does the ברייתא really follow רבי מאיר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10 רב said it plainly: the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. In this version a student raises it as a question, as if checking whether the ברייתא truly has to follow only that one opinion. The content is the same. Only the form changes, from a statement to a question.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion does this follow?

phrases.english: Some say:
phrases.notes: This tells us a second version of the conversation from Step 10 is coming.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rami bar Chama to Rav Chisda:
In accordance with whom? With Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם?
phrases.english: who says: a person can consecrate something that has not come into the world?
phrases.notes: This is the money from selling the bull, which does not exist yet (Step 9).

steps.triggerLanguage: איכא דאמרי, אמר ליה רב פפא לאביי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of Step 10, with רב's statement turned into a question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא must be following רבי מאיר's view that one can make holy something not yet in existence

steps.title: Answer: who else could it follow?
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that of course it follows רבי מאיר, since no other opinion fits.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Then whose view would it follow? It must be רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The teacher answers the question with a question of his own: 'Who else could it be?' In other words, yes, it is surely רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbis who argue with רבי מאיר hold that you cannot make holy something that does not exist yet. So the סיפא of the ברייתא, which makes holy the future sale money, can only fit רבי מאיר. The answer confirms Step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: Then like whom else? A way of saying the answer is obvious

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions the outcome is the same: the ברייתא about making holy the money from the bull's sale follows רבי מאיר, who holds that אדם מקדיש דבר שלא בא לעולם.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is the teacher answering: אביי in the first version, or רב חסדא in the second.

phrases.english: Rather, in accordance with whom else?
phrases.notes: He means: obviously רבי מאיר, since nobody else fits.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The ברייתא must follow רבי מאיר, since no other opinion allows making holy something that does not exist yet.

steps.title: Some attach the discussion to a ברייתא about a rented house
steps.stepSummary: Some taught this discussion on a different ברייתא. If a landlord's rented house gets נגעים and a כהן confirms it impure, the landlord can say 'yours is in front of you.' But once the house is torn down, he must give the renter another house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this discussion on the following ברייתא. If someone rents a house to his friend and it becomes afflicted with צרעת, even if a כהן confirmed it impure, the owner can say: 'Here is yours in front of you.' If the כהן tore it down, the owner must provide him a house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says some people placed the רבי מאיר discussion on a different ברייתא, and it quotes that ברייתא. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will ask whose view this ברייתא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the house still stands, even after a כהן declares it impure, the owner owes nothing more. The renter still has the house he rented. Once the house is torn down, the owner must give him a house. This raises a question about promising a house that is not there yet, which the גמרא will discuss next.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach this discussion on a different source
The house became afflicted with נגעי בתים (צרעת of houses)
The כהן declared it definitely impure
He tore it down
To provide him with a house

steps.confusionAlert: The house becoming impure does not cancel the rental by itself. As long as the house stands, the renter still has what he rented. Only when it is torn down must the owner give him another one.

phrases.english: And some teach it on this:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the whole discussion about רבי מאיר, now placed on a different ברייתא.

phrases.english: One who rents a house to his fellow, and it became afflicted with leprosy,
even though a priest confirmed it as impure,
he says to him: "Here, yours is before you."
If he dismantled it, he is obligated to provide him a house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another place where the רבי מאיר discussion was taught, and quotes that ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A landlord whose rented house gets נגעים may say 'yours is before you' while it stands, but once it is torn down he must provide another house.
